implementationAnalyses.conciseReason: The Content Agent document (finalAuthoringContract) explicitly authors a 'Hero Video' block (canonicalBlockName: hero-video, selector: div.herovideo, componentId: component-001) with a four-cell single-row table structure. The authored table header is 'Hero Video' and the single row contains four cells: [video asset], [heading text], [primary CTA link], [secondary CTA link]. Section metadata for this block's containing section provides subtitles, poster, and transcript as configurable assets — these are NOT block-table cells but section-metadata rows. The repository (ShubhadipChakrabarti/aem-boilerplate) has no blocks/herovideo directory; this is a net-new block. The live site loads /blocks/herovideo/herovideo.css confirming the canonical folder name is 'herovideo' (not 'hero-video'). The block must: (1) render a configurable video element using the authored video asset cell, (2) render the heading 'DISNEY IMAGINATION CAMPUS - STUDENT TRAVEL REIMAGINED' from cell 2, (3) render two CTA links 'PLAY FULL VIDEO' and 'LEARN MORE' from cells 3 and 4, (4) expose a visually-hidden playback helper text 'Press Enter or Space to play or pause the video.' for keyboard/screen-reader users matching the captured text, (5) support keyboard play/pause via Enter and Space on the video area, (6) treat poster, subtitles, and transcript as configurable via section-metadata (already authored in the Content Agent document's sectionMetadata array). Typography, color, hover, animation, spacing, and video source are NOT hardcoded per planning guardlines and uncaptured evidence list. The PLAY FULL VIDEO link carries aria-label 'PLAY FULL VIDEO about DISNEY IMAGINATION CAMPUS - STUDENT TRAVEL REIMAGINED' per the live computed-style sample, satisfying the accessibility criterion for clear accessible names.

implementationAnalyses.conciseReason: The Content Agent document (finalAuthoringContract) contains a grounded block entry for 'Cards (overlay)' with canonicalBlockName 'cards' and selector 'div.cards.overlay'. The authored table has two visible rows (PERFORMING ARTS and ARTS & HUMANITIES) but the live-page evidence confirms all four items (PERFORMING ARTS, ARTS & HUMANITIES, SCIENCE & TECHNOLOGY, LEADERSHIP & INNOVATION) are rendered by this same block instance (className 'cards overlay block size-4 clickable overlay-animation'). The story requires exactly those four items as interactive link-like items with configurable destinations. The repository already contains blocks/cards/cards.js and blocks/cards/cards.css (boilerplate implementation). The live site uses an 'overlay' variant class that the boilerplate cards block does not implement. The correct approach is to extend the existing cards block with an 'overlay' variant: add variant-specific CSS rules inside blocks/cards/cards.css and, if needed, minimal variant-aware JS logic inside blocks/cards/cards.js. No new block folder is created; the canonical EDS pattern for variants is a CSS class on the block header row (e.g. 'Cards (overlay)'). The authored table structure from the Content Agent is the authoritative HTML model: each row has three cells — [image/picture], [heading text], [link anchor] — matching the sourceText pattern 'PERFORMING ARTS https://...programs/performing-arts'. Because link targets were not captured for all four items, the JS decorator must read the href from the authored anchor in each row's third cell and fall back to '#' when absent, keeping destinations fully configurable by authors. Accessibility: each card item must be keyboard-reachable; the overlay variant renders items as full-card anchor elements so the <a> wrapping the card satisfies keyboard reachability and exposes the visible label as the accessible name. Ampersands in 'ARTS & HUMANITIES' and 'SCIENCE & TECHNOLOGY' are HTML-entity-encoded in the source (&) and must be decoded to their text equivalent in the accessible name — standard textContent retrieval handles this automatically.

implementationAnalyses.conciseReason: The repository already contains blocks/header/header.js and blocks/header/header.css (sha c7d6ea2 and 19d07bcf respectively). The existing implementation is a standard AEM boilerplate header that loads a /nav fragment and decorates it into brand, sections, and tools areas with hamburger mobile support. The story requires this block to render the Disney Imagination Campus-specific header content: a contact bar (Questions?, Call (321) 939 7560, Contact Us), the site logo/brand link, a search control, and five primary navigation items (ABOUT US, CURRICULUM & TICKETS, SPECIAL EVENTS, PLAN YOUR TRIP, CONNECT WITH US). The live computed-style evidence confirms the header renders at height 64px (matching --nav-height: 64px in styles.css), uses a fixed nav-wrapper with z-index 600, has a bottom border of 1px solid rgb(0,0,0) on the nav element, and the header text sample confirms all five nav labels and the contact content are present in the rendered DOM. The Content Agent document does NOT include a header block table — the header is a global/shared pattern loaded via the /nav fragment convention (header.js already calls loadFragment('/nav')). Per CONTENT GAP & UNGROUNDED BLOCK RULES, because the header is a global pattern loaded from a fragment document (/nav), the implementation must follow the existing EDS fragment-based nav convention: the /nav document is authored by the Content Agent and the header.js block decorates it. The block JS and CSS must be updated to support the Disney Imagination Campus nav document structure (contact bar row, brand row, sections row, tools/search row) while the /nav fragment document itself is a content-gap item for the Content Agent. The implementation must not hardcode uncaptured typography, spacing, colors, hover states, or link destinations. All configurable values (link hrefs, logo src) come from the authored /nav fragment. The existing header.css already provides the nav-wrapper, nav-brand, nav-sections, nav-hamburger, and nav-tools grid areas. The CSS must be extended to add a nav-contact area for the contact bar (Questions?, phone number, Contact Us link) and a nav-search area for the search control, both sourced from the /nav fragment. The JS must be updated to map the additional fragment sections to these new areas. The --nav-height CSS custom property in styles.css is 64px; the live evidence shows the header renders at exactly 64px, so no change to styles.css is needed unless the contact bar requires a taller header — but since the contact bar is observed within the same 64px header-wrapper rect (x:0 y:0 w:780 h:64), the existing height is sufficient for the captured viewport. The nav document convention maps fragment children by index: child[0]=brand, child[1]=sections, child[2]=tools. To add contact and search areas the JS must handle a 4- or 5-child fragment where child[0]=contact, child[1]=brand, child[2]=sections, child[3]=tools (search). This is the minimal safe change: extend the existing class-mapping array and add CSS for the new areas. No new block is created. No global styles.css token changes are required. The /nav fragment document structure is flagged as a content gap.
